title: GYM-QR
thesis: One session per member. One key per locker.
context: A gym records attendance in a paper book and hands out locker keys with no record of who holds them. I designed the system that replaces both, then wrote the requirements, the state rules and the acceptance tests before the code.
facts: 1,166 lines, personas, journeys, FR/NFR, DDL, API contract, decision log
Concept only, no gym owner, no deployment, no measured result

title: Prak_WebLanjut
thesis: The first time a request had to travel through a whole system.
context: Coursework for Web Lanjut: a Laravel application built commit by commit, a landing page, routes and views, then a form that posts and validates.
facts: Landing page, route and view layer, form handling
Where validation belongs when more than one screen is involved

title: UAS-DSP
thesis: Reading a dataset carefully enough to say what it does not prove.
context: Final exam notebook for digital signal processing: consumer price data, cleaning, comparison, and a written interpretation of what the numbers can and cannot support.
facts: Analysis notebook, prediction table, two source datasets
A conclusion is only as good as the column you did not check

title: pastebin
thesis: Designing the schema first made every interface decision obvious.
context: A paste service clone: a SQL schema, server routes and a Tailwind interface, built to understand what a small product needs before it needs features.
facts: The data model is the design document nobody reads until it is wrong
